task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the instrument-repair program at Nettleford College and the balance between giving students time to learn and getting school instruments back into use.

facts.text: A July 2026 workshop note records trainee Omi Keld fitting a clarinet pad, then taking the instrument to an instructor's inspection bench.
Nettleford College's one-year instrument-repair program enrolls 24 adult trainees from varied work and education backgrounds.
Participating school music departments supply instruments for supervised repair rather than buying a guaranteed express service.
Every returned instrument must pass an instructor's functional check under the program's stated process.
During the 2025–26 teaching year, the workshop accepted 180 school instruments and returned 150 after repair.
Twenty instruments were still awaiting parts at the year-end count, and ten were assessed as beyond the workshop's repair scope.
The figures count instruments, not distinct schools or trainee qualifications.
Under the program's fee schedule, schools pay a $35 handling contribution per accepted instrument, plus any agreed exceptional parts charge.
That payment does not cover the program's full teaching cost, which is supported by the college budget and a $20,000 annual grant.
A quoted commercial repair price for one comparable clarinet job was $120 with a shorter turnaround, not a price for every instrument.
The college normally asks schools to allow six weeks, with longer waits possible when parts are unavailable.
Band teacher Rella Brill uses spare instruments and changes rehearsal groups while pupils' instruments are away.
Brill said, "A cheaper repair is useful only if I can keep the student playing while we wait."
Keld previously repaired household appliances and says small changes in instrument adjustment require a different kind of checking.
Keld said, "The part can fit and the instrument can still tell you the job is not finished."
Instructor Teri Sorn says trainees sometimes repeat a task before it is accepted, adding learning time that a commercial quote may not allow.
The college has not published a matched study of long-term repair durability against commercial providers.
Completing the program provides a college certificate but not a guaranteed job or a promise that graduates can repair every instrument family.
The workshop shares a building with evening music classes, which use a separate set of instruments.
The next grant renewal is pending, and the current school contribution is not guaranteed to remain unchanged indefinitely.

forbidden_additions: The $35 fee covers all costs or all 180 instruments were repaired
